items.lawCode: Amd §66, Pub Serv L; amd §1020-f, Pub Auth L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8695

SPONSOR: CLEARE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law and the public authorities law,
in relation to requiring electric companies to provide alternative meas-
ures to ensure customers are able to maintain their health and well-be-
ing during power outages

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation would require that those electric customers who docu-
ment their need for essential electricity for medical needs will be
provided alternative measures to ensure their health and well-being if
power cannot adequately be provided.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subparagraph (iii) of paragraph (a) of subdivision 21
of section 66 of the public service law, as added by section 4 of part X
of chapter 57 of the laws of 2013 to require that those electric custom-
ers who document their need for essential electricity for medical needs
will be provided alternative measures to ensure their health and wellbe-
ing if power cannot adequately be provided.  These provisions include
electric generators or lodging for the individual as well as transporta-
tion of their medical devices as needed. This section also clarifies
that any cost incurred shall not be borne by rate payers.

Section 2 amends paragraph 1 of subdivision (cc) of section 1020-f of
the public authorities law, as added by section 7 of part A of chapter
173 of the laws of 2013 requiring service providers' emergency response
plans to include provisions regarding how customers will be provided
with alternate measures to ensure their health and well-being if power
cannot adequately be provided. These provisions include electric genera-
tors or lodging for any individual as well as transportation of their
medical devices as needed.

Section 3 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under law, electric companies are required to identify and have an
outreach plan for customers who have documented their need for essential
electricity due to their medical needs, however there is no priority
guarantee of power restoration. This legislation seeks to provide alter-
native measures to these individuals who are dependent on electricity to
meet their medical needs. Superstorm Sandy, Tropical Storm Isaias and
Hurricane Ida have shown us the critical need for fail-safe measures to
be in place to save these individuals lives. This legislation ensures
that if a power outage occurs and that outage will impact the health and
well-being of a medically needy individual there are other means to
continue their necessary treatment. Simply put, this legislation will
save lives.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-20: A11017-Referred to corporations, authorities and commissions

2021-22: A3042-Referred to corporations, authorities and commissions

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires electric companies to provide alternative measures to ensure customers with documented need for essential electricity for medical needs have access to electricity during power outages; requires electric companies to provide generators or lodging for such individuals and transportation for medical devices.
